statute_note: Principal source: the LankaLaw consolidated HTML (chain block 'Ordinance Nos, 12 of 1840 12 of 1840 22 of 1931 8 of 1847 Act Nos, 8 of 1854'), parsed by build_canonical_statutes.py into a 10-section tree with paragraphs (a) to (c) and closing words in s.7 and one definition in s.10; no provisos, subsections or schedules. Other sources inspected: the registry's compendium PDF (1980 revised edition volume 5, Cap. 288 at PDF pp. 170 to 171, chain 'Ordinances Nos.l2ofl840, 22 of 1931, 8 of 1947, Act No. 8 of 1954.'), used as the verification source; the finalized State Lands Ordinance (8 of 1947) package; the amendments folder listing. Consolidation cutoff: unknown. The two copies disagree on the years of the second and third amending instruments (1847/1854 in the HTML against 1947/1954 in the compendium); neither carries an inline marker; nothing held settles it. Both readings are quoted in the manifest and in the tree's amendment_chain_conflict. Review performed: every section number, marginal note and the full text of all ten sections, three paragraphs and the definition compared word for word against the compendium text layer and its rendered pages; the two copies agree throughout apart from 'wilful'/'willful' (ss.2 and 9, corrected to the compendium spelling with raw_text kept) and the s.3 note's final period (added, heading_raw kept). validate_finalized_trees.py reports 0 errors and 0 warnings. Amendment coverage: three instruments known from the headers, none held; each has one reconciliation row; nothing applied. OCR or structural weaknesses: the HTML chain block is visibly damaged (duplicated '12 of 1840' row); the compendium's own header reads 'Nos.l2ofl840'. Both copies are LankaLaw republications; the compendium is not an independent print. Missing sources: a Government Printer print of Cap. 288 or of any of the amending instruments. Unresolved questions: which chain reading is correct; whether Ordinance No. 8 of 1947 (the State Lands Ordinance) is the second amending instrument. Status: needs_structural_review, because two held copies disagree on a material field (the chain) and no held source resolves it. The section text itself is not in doubt between the two copies. Lawyer verification: unverified.
